title: “Let the Sunshine In”: The Impact of Industry Payment Disclosure on Physician Prescription Behavior
authors: Tong Guo; Srinivasaraghavan Sriram; Puneet Manchanda
eligible_reason: Not a staggered design, and the outcome is simulated. Only Massachusetts' disclosure law is studied, a single state and a single date (post1), with physicians in border areas as controls. The treatment is split into brand and generic interactions (two treatment regressors). Every column adds time-varying zip-level controls (monthly enrolled members, log median income, percent private and public insurance). The FE set is brand x physician plus year-month x brand x border-area.
design_notes: regression_simulate_data.do: areg y_sim MAxT1xbrand MAxT1xgeneric timetrend##branddummy##borderD c.monthlymemberno c.loginc_median c.pctprivate c.pctpublic, absorb(ib_num) vce(cluster npi), run for the statin, antidepressant and antipsychotic classes. Physician-heterogeneity regressions follow with further interactions.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. The README says the dataset is simulated: confidential X variables are rescaled and Y is simulated from the authors' model estimates.
